title: hook-risk manifest
description:
A risk assessment of one Uniswap v4 hook, bound to one exact deployment.

The binding is the point. A manifest describes a (chainId, address, codehash) triple, and a manifest whose codehash no longer matches the code at that address describes something that no longer exists. That is why upgradeability raises a hook's tier: an upgradeable hook cannot carry a durable assessment, because any assessment is invalidated by the next upgrade.

Every number in here says where it came from. `measured` values were observed from code or chain state; `declared` values were asserted by the team; `unmeasured` means nobody knows, which is deliberately not the same as zero.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this schema. Consumers should reject unknown majors.

generatedAt.description: Omitted in reproducible builds so two runs over the same input produce byte-identical manifests.

commandLine.description: Invocation, so a reader can reproduce the run.

target.description: What was assessed. Exactly one of `source` or `deployed` is required; a manifest may carry both when a deployed hook has verified source.

mode.description: `source` scans a local Foundry project. `deployed` works from bytecode at an address. `deployed-with-source` is both, and is the only mode that can reconcile declared permissions against the address bits.

codehash.description: keccak256 of the deployed runtime code. The manifest is valid for this value and no other.

blockNumber.description: Block the deployed state was read at, so the assessment is pinned in time.

sourceAvailable.description: False when the explorer had no verified source. Every finding derived from source analysis is then absent, and findings from bytecode carry reduced confidence.

permissions.description: The hook's 14 permission bits, from up to three sources that can disagree — which is the whole subject of detector HS-02.

fromAddress.description: Decoded from the low 14 bits of the deployed address. This is what the PoolManager actually obeys.

fromSource.description: Declared by getHookPermissions(). The author's stated intent.

implemented.description: Callbacks with a working implementation. A callback that only reverts is not implemented.

divergences.description: Where the three disagree. Non-empty means either dead code or a bricked pool operation.

invariants.description: Results from the differential harness. Absent when the dynamic layer did not run.

id.description: I1 conservation and solvency, I2 no undeclared extraction, I3 exit liveness.

status.description: `inconclusive` means the run was cut short and is deliberately distinct from `passed`. `not-applicable` is I2 against a custom-curve hook, where output comparison against an unhooked pool is meaningless by construction.

counterexample.description: The shrunk sequence that reproduces a failure.

revertSelector.description: The hook's own error, unwrapped from v4's ERC-7751 WrappedError.

revertRaw.description: The revert exactly as the PoolManager produced it, wrapper included.

total.description: Sum over dimensions with a known value. Unmeasured dimensions are excluded, never counted as zero.

totalUpperBound.description: Total if every unmeasured dimension were at its maximum.

inconclusive.description: True when missing data leaves the tier undetermined between `tier` and `tierUpperBound`.

revision.description: Commit of uniswapfoundation/security-framework this scoring follows. A score is only meaningful against a stated revision.

source.description: `measured` was observed by hookrisk. `declared` was asserted by the team and cannot be checked. Conflating the two is how a self-assessment acquires unearned authority.

bracketsAreInterpretation.description: True when hookrisk supplies the brackets because the framework publishes none for this dimension. Seven of nine are in this state; see FEEDBACK.md #2.

triggers.description: Feature triggers that fired. These apply regardless of tier — the framework's own defence against a team scoring itself low.

derivationIsInterpretation.description: True when the dimension-to-trigger link is hookrisk's reading rather than the framework's. See FEEDBACK.md #5.

sources.description: Every tier or trigger that asked for this action, and how strongly. Kept so a report can explain why an action is required rather than merely stating it.

engines.description: Every analysis engine hookrisk attempted, including those that were skipped. A skipped engine is recorded so a reader can tell 'nothing was found' apart from 'nothing looked'.

upstream.description: Attribution for third-party engines. Running someone else's tool and saying so is the minimum.

coverage.description: What the analysis did and did not reach. Reporting a clean scan without this is how a tool converts its own blind spots into false assurance.

corroboratedFindings.description: Findings confirmed by more than one analysis foundation.

uncoveredFunctions.description: Functions static analysis could not lift to IR and therefore never examined. See error HR-E205.

gate.description: Outcome of the CI gate, when one was configured.

permissionSet.description: The 14 hook permissions. Field names match Hooks.Permissions in v4-core.

id.description: Stable across runs: derived from rule class, location and function, never from the reporting engine.

ruleClass.description: Canonical taxonomy shared across engines, so the same defect found by two tools is one finding rather than two.

confidence.description: Promoted to `high` when engines built on different analysis foundations agree.

isClassification.description: True for findings that describe a design choice rather than a defect, such as custom accounting. These affect scoring; they are not things to fix.

nativeRule.description: The engine's own rule name, kept so a user can trace a finding back to its source tool.
